sections.heading: Explore races by level of government
sections.intro: Your exact ballot depends on where you live. Each category below has a concise explanation and the right official source

cards.title: US House
cards.body: Congressional contests are determined by your district. Use your voter address to confirm the congressional district and contest that apply to you. The California certified candidate list provides the official statewide roster for the November General Election.

cards.title: Statewide Offices
cards.body: Governor and statewide constitutional offices appear across California. The November ballot includes Governor and other statewide constitutional offices as certified by the California Secretary of State. Use the official Voter Information Guide for statewide candidate and proposition information.

cards.title: State Legislature
cards.body: State Senate and Assembly contests depend on your district. Use the official district lookup to confirm which State Senate and Assembly contests apply to your address. The California certified candidate list provides the official November candidate roster.

cards.title: County Ballot
cards.body: County-administered contests and district races vary by address. Santa Barbara County administers the November election and publishes current local election information, ballot resources and district-specific material. Confirm the districts connected to your voter address before reviewing local contests.

cards.title: Santa Barbara
cards.body: Mayor and City Council Districts 4, 5 and 6 are on the November ballot. Santa Barbara voters will elect a Mayor and representatives for Districts 4, 5 and 6. Use the City of Santa Barbara Elections page and official candidate list for the current municipal election record. SBWPC endorsement decisions are maintained separately on the Endorsements page.

cards.title: School + Special Districts
cards.body: Education and special-district contests depend on your voter address. Use the County district lookup and November General Election page to confirm the local governing-board contests that apply to you. SBWPC endorsement decisions are maintained separately on the Endorsements page.

cards.title: Ballot Measures
cards.body: State propositions and local measures may appear on your ballot. Use the California Official Voter Information Guide for statewide propositions and Santa Barbara County Elections for local measures.

Laura has built on her decades of experience to tackle the urgent and interconnected issues of today: housing, homelessness, drought and climate change, mental health, economic development, transportation, healthcare and public safety, while creating innovative solutions for the issues of tomorrow. She's worked hard to make sure our county delivers services to keep us safe and protect our quality of life.

Melinda Greene has served Santa Barbara County for nearly 30 years, beginning as a CPA in the Auditor-Controller’s office. She later worked as a Budget Analyst and Certified Public Finance Officer in the County Executive Office. Since 2003, she has held leadership roles in IT and currently serves as Chief Deputy Clerk-Recorder and CFO. An Advanced Certified Appraiser and Certified Elections Registration Administrator, Melinda has supported elections since 1998 and served as a County Public Information Officer during emergencies since 2000. She holds a degree in Business Economics from UCSB.

Kyle Slattery, a lifelong resident of Santa Barbara County, is a CPA and a seasoned public sector leader. His extensive experience spans public accounting and government, including over a decade in the Auditor-Controller’s Office, where he held the position of Chief Deputy Controller. Currently, he serves as the Deputy Chief Information Officer, where he spearheads the modernization of County enterprise systems to enhance efficiency. His campaign emphasizes experienced, professional leadership, transparency, accountability, and the establishment of effective systems.

sections.heading: What the forms tell you
sections.intro: Different filings document different stages and types of campaign financial activity

cards.title: Candidate intention statement
cards.body: Identifies a candidate's intention to seek elected office and is generally filed before campaign fundraising or spending begins

cards.title: Statement of organization
cards.body: Identifies a recipient committee and provides information about how the campaign committee is organized

cards.title: Recipient committee campaign statement
cards.body: Reports contributions received, expenditures made, cash balances and other reportable campaign financial activity

cards.title: Candidate campaign short form
cards.body: Used by candidates who do not have a controlled committee and remain below the applicable campaign activity threshold

cards.title: 24-hour independent expenditure report
cards.body: Reports qualifying independent expenditures that are made separately from spending controlled by a candidate campaign

cards.title: 24-hour contribution report
cards.body: Reports qualifying contributions during periods when accelerated campaign disclosure requirements apply

sections.heading: What to look for
sections.intro: Campaign filings serve different purposes and may appear at different stages of a campaign

cards.title: Start with the form
cards.body: The form number tells you what kind of campaign activity is being reported

cards.title: Check the filing date
cards.body: More recent filings can reflect activity that occurred after an earlier report

cards.title: Review multiple filings
cards.body: Looking across several reports can help show changes in contributions and campaign activity over time

cards.title: Separate candidate and outside spending
cards.body: Independent expenditures are separate from spending controlled by a candidate campaign committee

cards.title: Verify the official record
cards.body: Each filing displayed here is connected to the official public campaign filing record
